title: American Art
description: From frontier light to mid-century city scenes — the American eye.

items.title: Sideboard
items.medium: Ebonized mahogany with glass and silvered brass
items.description_narrative: This elegant sideboard, designed by Edward William Godwin, is crafted from ebonized mahogany, glass, and silvered brass. Its streamlined form reflects the aesthetic innovations of its period.
items.tags: furniture, sideboard, design, victorian, english, decorative arts, ebonized mahogany

items.title: Ideal Pastoral Life
items.description_narrative: Edward Calvert's 'Ideal Pastoral Life' is a woodcut print depicting a tranquil, idealized rural scene. This work captures a serene vision of nature and human harmony, characteristic of a pastoral theme.
items.tags: pastoral, rural, idealism, woodcut, printmaking, serene, nature

items.title: A Holiday
items.description_narrative: Edward Henry Potthast's "A Holiday" captures a vibrant scene of leisure, executed in oil on canvas with a distinctive luminist touch. The work exemplifies his well-known focus on depicting everyday life and recreational moments, often featuring figures enjoying a spirited atmosphere.
items.tags: holiday, leisure, genre painting, American Impressionism, oil painting, figures, vibrant, recreational

items.title: Elaine
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts Elaine, a character from Alfred Lord Tennyson's 'Idylls of the King'. Toby Edward Rosenthal's work captures a poignant moment from the Arthurian legend.
items.tags: narrative painting, Victorian art, Arthurian legend, tragedy, oil painting, 19th century

items.title: Sleeping Infant Faun Visited by an Inquisitive Rabbit
items.description_narrative: Edward Clark Potter's marble sculpture, "Sleeping Infant Faun Visited by an Inquisitive Rabbit," depicts a mythological creature in a moment of tranquil slumber. The work charmingly captures a scene of quiet curiosity as a small rabbit gently approaches the sleeping faun.
items.tags: faun, rabbit, marble sculpture, mythological, tranquil, naturalistic, 19th century, whimsical

items.title: George Washington
items.description_narrative: This striking portrait captures George Washington, a pivotal figure in American history, during his presidency. Painted by Edward Savage, it serves as an important historical document and a testament to the nation's early identity.
items.tags: portrait, american history, founding father, oil painting, 18th century, formal, dignified

items.title: Cupid's Hunting Fields
items.medium: Gouache, with watercolor and gold and silver paints on ivory wove paper, laid down on linen canvas
items.description_narrative: Sir Edward Burne-Jones's 'Cupid's Hunting Fields,' created in 1885, exemplifies the artist's distinctive style and thematic interests. This intricate work utilizes gouache, watercolor, and metallic paints to evoke a dreamlike or allegorical scene.
items.tags: pre-raphaelite, symbolism, mythology, allegory, dreamlike, decorative, romantic, british art

items.title: The Ploughman
items.description_narrative: Edward Calvert's 1827 woodcut, "The Ploughman," depicts a figure tilling the land, embodying a pastoral simplicity. The artist's meticulous hand is evident in the finely detailed linework characteristic of early 19th-century printmaking.
items.tags: rural, labor, woodcut, landscape, figure, british art, pastoral

items.title: The Herring Net
items.description_narrative: This oil painting depicts two fishermen in a dory, diligently hauling a teeming herring net from the turbulent Atlantic waters. Winslow Homer masterfully captures the raw power of the sea and the arduous labor required for survival.
items.tags: maritime, fishing, realism, american art, sea, labor, nature, atlantic

items.title: After the Hurricane, Bahamas
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on moderately thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "After the Hurricane, Bahamas" is a powerful watercolor depicting the aftermath of a storm in the Bahamas. Created in 1899, this work showcases Homer's masterful use of transparent and opaque watercolor to convey the scene's atmosphere and texture.
items.tags: seascape, storm aftermath, bahamas, nature, realism, 19th century art

items.title: Croquet Scene
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'Croquet Scene' captures a moment of leisure from 1866. This oil on canvas depicts figures engaged in a game of croquet, characteristic of American life in the post-Civil War era.
items.tags: croquet, leisure, genre scene, american art, oil painting, 19th century, figures

items.title: The Water Fan
items.medium: Watercolor, with blotting and touches of scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough twill-textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "The Water Fan" (1898/99) showcases the artist's exceptional command of watercolor. He skillfully utilized blotting and scraping over a graphite drawing on thick, twill-textured paper, capturing the dynamic essence of moving water.
items.tags: american art, watercolor, marine art, realism, nature, late 19th century, landscape

items.title: The Gulf Stream
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor and traces of blotting, over graphite, on moderately thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper (lower edge trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'The Gulf Stream' dramatically portrays a lone figure on a dismasted boat, surrounded by sharks, against the vast, indifferent power of the sea. Executed primarily in transparent watercolor, this work exemplifies Homer's profound engagement with the natural world and themes of survival.
items.tags: marine art, American Realism, sea, struggle, solitude, dramatic, ocean

items.title: Life-Size Black Bass
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper (left, right and lower edges trimmed)
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's "Life-Size Black Bass" depicts the titular fish with remarkable detail, capturing its form and scales. Executed in 1904, this watercolor showcases Homer's mastery of the medium through techniques like rewetting, blotting, and scraping.
items.tags: black bass, fish, wildlife, watercolor, realism, nature, american art

items.title: Stowing Sail
items.medium: Transparent watercolor, with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting, scraping and graphite, on thick, moderately textured (twill texture on verso), ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer captures the strenuous act of sailors stowing a sail, emphasizing the dynamic interaction between man and the powerful forces of the sea. Executed in 1903, this watercolor demonstrates Homer's mastery of the medium through techniques like rewetting, blotting, and scraping to depict the rough texture of the ocean and the vessel.
items.tags: marine, seascape, watercolor, american, realism, nautical, early 20th century

items.title: North Woods Club, Adirondacks (The Interrupted Tete-a-Tete)
items.medium: Watercolor, with rewetting, blotting and scraping, over graphite, on thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Winslow Homer's 'North Woods Club, Adirondacks' captures a serene moment within the dense wilderness. Executed in 1892 with watercolor, the work showcases his mastery of the medium to depict the rugged American landscape.
items.tags: nature, landscape, watercolor, adirondacks, american art, realism, 19th century, outdoors

items.title: The Fountain, Villa Torlonia, Frascati, Italy
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1907 oil on canvas depicts a serene fountain within the elaborate gardens of Villa Torlonia in Frascati, Italy. The artist masterfully captures the play of light and shadow, highlighting the architectural grandeur and natural beauty of the Italian landscape.
items.tags: fountain, villa, garden, italy, landscape, oil painting, light, serene

items.title: Mrs. George Swinton (Elizabeth Ebsworth)
items.description_narrative: This striking oil portrait by John Singer Sargent depicts Mrs. George Swinton, Elizabeth Ebsworth, in a formal setting. Sargent's masterful brushwork captures her poise and the luxurious details of her attire.
items.tags: portrait, woman, oil painting, realism, gilded age, late 19th century, society portraiture, elegant

items.title: Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent, a master of late 19th-century portraiture, captures Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre) with an air of refined elegance. Painted in oil on canvas in 1882, this work showcases Sargent's characteristic ability to convey both the sitter's personality and their social standing.
items.tags: portrait, society portrait, oil painting, realism, 19th century, american art, elegance

items.title: Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 'Life Study (Study of an Egyptian Girl)' captures a figure with remarkable immediacy and detail, characteristic of the artist's masterful draftsmanship and use of oil paint. This work exemplifies Sargent's approach to portraiture and figure studies, emphasizing the presence and form of his subjects.
items.tags: life study, portrait, oil painting, figure study, realism, american art, 19th century
